people.name: Victor Kasonde
people.notes: Lead guitarist and vocalist, Broken String. House band at The Copperbelt Room on Cha Cha Cha Road. Radio Zambia broadcast the band twice in the past year. A third session was being negotiated at the time of death.

people.name: Grace Mwape
people.notes: Co-owner of The Copperbelt Room. Manages the club accounts. Attended Evelyn Hone College. Married to Arthur Mwape.

people.name: Arthur Mwape
people.notes: Co-owner of The Copperbelt Room. Public-facing partner. Handles relations with musicians, press, and the licensing board. Does not manage the accounts.

people.name: Bernard Chanda
people.notes: Senior Director of Finance, NCCM (Nchanga Consolidated Copper Mines). Member, UNIP National Council, Lusaka Province. Drives a grey Mercedes-Benz 220.

people.name: Solomon Musonda
people.notes: Owner, Musonda Transport. Three trucks on the Lusaka-Ndola corridor. Extends informal personal loans. Known to the precinct for two prior disputes, both resolved.

people.name: Patrick Kabwe
people.notes: Rhythm guitarist, The Copper Kings. Had a public argument with Victor Kasonde on 11 November 1974 over a disputed song composition. Witnesses present.

people.name: Agnes Lungu
people.notes: Victor Kasonde's girlfriend of fourteen months. Works at a legal firm on Cairo Road. Had been asking questions at the club in the days before the murder.

people.name: Chilufya Nsofu
people.notes: Head bouncer, The Copperbelt Room. Three years at the club. Was absent from his post between approximately 22:10 and 22:40 on the night of the murder.

people.name: Choolwe Mutale
people.notes: Victor Kasonde's informal booking agent. Arranged Radio Zambia session negotiations and club circuit bookings. Had a dispute with Kasonde over an unpaid commission of 40 kwacha.

people.name: Blessings Mwanza
people.notes: Head bartender, The Copperbelt Room. Three years at the club. Witnessed the argument between Kabwe and Kasonde on 11 November. On duty the night of the murder.

people.name: Enos Simukonda
people.notes: Club caretaker and night cleaner. Found the body of Victor Kasonde in the rear alley at approximately 01:40 on 15 November 1974.

people.name: Joanna Zulu
people.notes: Recording coordinator, Radio Zambia. Was negotiating a full studio session and possible vinyl pressing for Broken String. Met with Kasonde privately twice in the week before his death.

people.name: Elizabeth Kasonde
people.notes: Victor Kasonde's older sister. Teaches at a primary school in Kabulonga. Next of kin. Notified by DC Mwamba at 06:15 on 15 November 1974.

people.name: Emmanuel Banda
people.notes: Bassist, Broken String. Victor Kasonde's closest bandmate. Reported to CID on 15 November that a guitar E-string was missing from the band's supply case. String had been present at the previous rehearsal on 12 November.

people.name: Chibesa Mwamba
people.notes: Detective Constable, CID Lusaka. First officer to secure the crime scene at The Copperbelt Room. Took initial statements from Nsofu, Mwanza, and Simukonda.

people.name: Boyd Sikazwe
people.notes: Music correspondent, Times of Zambia. Has written two profiles of Broken String, the most recent published August 1974. Was not at the club on the night of the murder.

people.name: Joseph Mwale
people.notes: Former bassist. Disappeared September 1972. Missing persons case 72/LKS/0891. Never resolved. Last known address: Chilenje. No body found, no explanation given.

people.name: Francis Bwalya
people.notes: Detective Inspector, CID Lusaka. Seven years in service. Handles commercial and market-related cases. Assigned to Kamwala district disputes.

people.name: Rajan Patel
people.notes: Co-owner, Patel Brothers Import Wholesale, Kamwala market. Imports dry goods, hardware, and textiles. Third-generation business.

people.name: Suresh Patel
people.notes: Co-owner, Patel Brothers Import Wholesale, Kamwala market. Handles logistics and supplier relations.

people.name: Temwani Phiri
people.notes: Bar back, The Copperbelt Room. Seventeen years old. Reported seeing a woman follow Kasonde toward the rear exit at approximately 22:10 on the night of the murder. Did not see her face clearly.

interviews.location: The Copperbelt Room, 12 Cha Cha Cha Road
interviews.statement: I finished mopping the back corridor at around half past one in the morning. When I pushed open the alley door — the one by the stage store — I nearly tripped. A man was lying face down between the bins and the wall. I called out. No movement. I ran inside and found Chilufya at the front and told him to call the police. I did not touch the body. The alley door latch was already up when I reached it. I assumed someone had left it open for air.

interviews.location: The Copperbelt Room, 12 Cha Cha Cha Road
interviews.statement: My post is the front entrance. I was there until around ten past ten. Then Mrs Mwape — Grace Mwape — came to me personally. She said there was a delivery man at the service gate who needed escorting out. She gave me fifty ngwee and said she would watch the front door for twenty minutes. I went to the service gate. There was no one there. I waited, then walked around to the rear alley. Nothing. I came back to my post at about twenty to eleven. Mrs Mwape was gone from the front by then. I assumed she had returned to her office.

interviews.location: The Copperbelt Room, 12 Cha Cha Cha Road
interviews.statement: Kasonde came to the bar around nine, between sets. He seemed anxious — kept glancing toward the back corridor. He had one Mosi and went back. Later, around ten or ten past, I saw Mrs Mwape walking toward the back corridor. That is normal — the office is that way. I did not see her come back. The bar was busy. At around twenty past ten the band returned to the stage without Kasonde. Emmanuel told the room he was taking a short break. That was not normal. Kasonde never missed an entrance.

interviews.location: The Copperbelt Room, 12 Cha Cha Cha Road
interviews.statement: I was carrying empties from the rear bar to the store corridor at around ten past ten. I saw Mr Kasonde go through the internal door at the end of the corridor — the one that leads to the rear alley. A minute or two later, a woman followed him through the same door. I did not see her face. She wore a dark dress, blue or black. Medium height, not young. I thought nothing of it at the time. I assumed it was one of the owners.

Victor and I have played together for three years. He never walked off mid-set without telling me. When he did not come back for the second half I thought he had too much to drink, or a problem with his guitar. On the fifteenth, when I heard what had happened, I went straight to the equipment case. We keep spare E-strings — Victor breaks them at least once a month. There should have been four in the case. There were three. I last confirmed all four were there on the twelfth of November at our rehearsal.

Victor telephoned me on the tenth. He said he was in a complicated situation involving someone at the club. He would not say more. He said he was going to resolve it and I should not worry. I told him to be careful with the people he was dealing with. He could be too clever for his own good sometimes. When you told me he had been strangled, my first thought was: that is close work. Someone he trusted, or someone who got very close to him.

I was at the UNZA Nice bar from about half past eight until after midnight. I was with my cousin, Priscilla Banda — she is a second-year student there. Victor and I had argued that week. He was keeping something from me. I thought at first it was another woman. Now I think it was something more serious than that. He was frightened. Victor was not the type to be frightened easily. You can speak to Priscilla.

I have been in Livingstone since the twelfth. Three trucks on a southern route contract — copper fittings for the railway line. I came back on the sixteenth when I heard the news. Victor owed me five hundred kwacha — borrowed in November of last year for some equipment. He paid me back on the fourteenth. His bank transferred it while I was in Livingstone. I had half written the debt off. I had no reason to want him dead. A dead man repays nothing.

I was not at the club that evening. I had dinner at the Pamodzi Hotel with clients from Kitwe — mineral rights people. Grace handles the evening operations. She always has. She telephoned me around eleven to say there had been an incident and police had been called. I drove down immediately. She told me about Kasonde in the car park. She was very composed. Grace is always composed, of course — but that night, even for her, she was very composed.

I was in the office from approximately half past nine reviewing accounts. I did not leave the office during that time. I spoke briefly to Chilufya in the corridor around ten — I asked him to check the service gate, which has been giving trouble. I did not go to the rear alley. I did not follow anyone. Kasonde was our house-band musician. We had a straightforward professional relationship. I have no knowledge of why anyone would wish him harm.

I was at the Ridgeway Hotel restaurant from about seven until after ten. I was meeting Emmanuel Nkonde — he is promotions manager at Radio Zambia — to discuss future session arrangements for the band. He can confirm. As for Victor: yes, we had a disagreement over a commission. Forty kwacha. He had a different view of what we had agreed. It was not a large sum. I was not going to harm a man over forty kwacha.

crime_scene_reports.description: Victim found lying face down between waste bins and the rear wall of the premises. Ligature mark around neck consistent with strangulation by thin wire. No signs of struggle beyond perimortem marks. Rear alley door found unlatched from inside — latch is operated from the corridor side only. Single set of fresh heel impressions in compacted dirt adjacent to body, smaller than victim's footwear, possibly female. No weapon recovered at scene.

Search of victim's residence at 14B Bwacha Road, Northmead. One-bedroom flat, no signs of disturbance. Personal papers searched. Recovered one handwritten note (evidence item 4) found inside a book on the bedroom shelf. Note reads: 'Agreed amount monthly, first of each month, until I say otherwise. If you stop I speak to Arthur.' Unsigned. Flat otherwise unremarkable.

evidence.description: Single guitar E-string wire, approximately 65 centimetres, found around the victim's neck post-mortem. Light gauge, consistent with commercial guitar strings. Identified by Emmanuel Banda as matching the type used by Broken String. One string of this type found missing from the band's supply case — last confirmed present on 12 November.

Single partial heel impression in compacted dirt, adjacent to body. Approximately 7 centimetres width. Inconsistent with victim's footwear (size 11 boot). Estimate: female shoe, size 5 to 6. Photographed. Cast not taken due to dry conditions.

Alley-side internal door found in unlatched position when scene was examined. Latch mechanism is operated from the corridor side only — it cannot be opened from the alley without a key. Indicates the door was opened from inside by someone with access to the back corridor.

Note reads: 'Agreed amount monthly, first of each month, until I say otherwise. If you stop I speak to Arthur.' Unsigned. Found inside a copy of 'The African Child' on the victim's bedroom shelf. Handwriting analysis requested. The reference to 'Arthur' may indicate the writer feared exposure to someone named Arthur.

Cash box from the club manager's office reviewed at DC Mwamba's request. Physical cash and ledger balance in agreement at K1,340. However, cross-reference with the club's Standard Chartered bank statements reveals repeated unexplained withdrawals over eighteen months, totalling approximately K6,500. All withdrawals are recorded under maintenance and equipment headings. No corresponding contractor receipts found on file.
evidence.location_found: Club manager's office, The Copperbelt Room

sightings.notes: Woman in dark dress observed following Victor Kasonde through the internal corridor door toward the rear of the club. Witness did not see her face clearly. Described as medium height, not young. Consistent with Grace Mwape's build and attire that evening per other witness accounts.
Kabwe seen at the Ridgeway Lounge bar at approximately 20:30. The Copper Kings were performing that evening. Confirmed by multiple venue staff and band members.
Kabwe still present at the Ridgeway Lounge at end of the Copper Kings set, approximately 23:00. Alibi confirmed by venue staff and band members. Kabwe could not have been at The Copperbelt Room.
Agnes Lungu at the UNZA Nice bar from approximately 20:30. Present with her cousin, Priscilla Banda, a second-year student. Remained until after midnight. Alibi confirmed by cousin and venue staff.
Choolwe Mutale at the Ridgeway Hotel restaurant from approximately 19:30 until after 22:00. Meeting with Emmanuel Nkonde, Radio Zambia Promotions. Confirmed by Nkonde and restaurant staff.

Musonda confirmed in Livingstone on the day of the murder. Presence verified by delivery receipts, truck driver statements, and telephone exchange records showing a call from the Livingstone exchange at 09:00.
Grey Mercedes-Benz 220 with plate LSK 4412 observed parked outside The Copperbelt Room at approximately 18:00. Vehicle is registered to Bernard Chanda. Chanda not seen entering the premises.

newspaper_archive.headline: Musician Found Dead at City Centre Club
newspaper_archive.body: A 27-year-old musician was found dead in the rear alley of The Copperbelt Room on Cha Cha Cha Road in the early hours of Friday morning. Victor Kasonde, lead guitarist of popular Lusaka group Broken String, was discovered by club staff at approximately 01:40. Police have confirmed the death is being treated as suspicious. Detective Constable Chibesa Mwamba of the CID confirmed that enquiries are ongoing. The club has been temporarily closed. No arrests have been made.

newspaper_archive.headline: Broken String: The Sound of Copper Town
newspaper_archive.body: In a first-floor rehearsal room off Cairo Road, four young men are building something. Broken String — led by guitarist Victor Kasonde, 27, from Northmead — plays a style that fuses Zambian township rhythms with electric lines that would not be out of place in Lagos or Kinshasa. 'We are making Zambian music for Zambia,' says Kasonde. 'Not copying anyone.' Radio Zambia has broadcast the group twice in the past twelve months. A third session, and possibly a vinyl pressing, is under negotiation. Broken String performs regularly at The Copperbelt Room on Cha Cha Cha Road, Thursday and Saturday evenings.

newspaper_archive.headline: Missing: Joseph Mwale, Musician, Last Seen Chilenje
newspaper_archive.body: The family of Joseph Mwale, 30, requests any information regarding his whereabouts. Mr Mwale, known as Joze, was a bass guitarist with several Lusaka musical groups. He was last seen in the Chilenje area on or around 20 September 1972. Described as tall, of medium build, with close-cropped hair. Anyone with information should contact CID Lusaka or the family directly. Case reference: 72/LKS/0891.

newspaper_archive.headline: No Arrest in Cha Cha Cha Road Murder
newspaper_archive.body: Three days after the death of musician Victor Kasonde at The Copperbelt Room, CID Lusaka has confirmed no arrests have been made. A spokesperson said enquiries are continuing and the investigation is active. Kasonde, the lead guitarist of Broken String, was found strangled in the club's rear alley in the early hours of 15 November. Bandmates and family have paid tribute. The club remains temporarily closed.

precinct_logs.notes: 01:52 — Called to The Copperbelt Room, 12 Cha Cha Cha Road. Body of male found in rear alley by club caretaker. Victim identified as Victor Kasonde, 14B Bwacha Road, Northmead. Scene secured. Initial statements taken from E. Simukonda (caretaker), B. Mwanza (bartender), T. Phiri (bar back), C. Nsofu (bouncer). Evidence log opened. CID notified at 02:20.

06:15 — Next of kin notified. Elizabeth Kasonde, 11A Leopards Hill Road, Kabulonga. 09:30 — Search of victim's flat, 14B Bwacha Road, Northmead. Handwritten note recovered, logged as evidence item 4. Note references an agreed monthly payment and a person named Arthur. Flat otherwise undisturbed.

Case 72/LKS/0891. Joseph Mwale, male, 30, musician, last known address Chilenje. Last seen approximately 20 September 1972. No physical evidence of foul play at last known address. Subject known to travel between Lusaka, Ndola, and Livingstone for musical engagements. Enquiries initiated with Ndola and Livingstone divisions.

Case 72/LKS/0891 — progress note. No trace of Mwale found. Ndola and Livingstone divisions returned negative enquiries. No known associates have heard from him. Chilenje address vacated. File remains open.

Case 72/LKS/0891 — Mwale. Supervisor review completed. Insufficient grounds for continued active investigation. No evidence of crime. Subject may have departed voluntarily. Classification changed to inactive. File retained on record.

relationships.notes: Married 1956. Co-owners of The Copperbelt Room. Arthur is the public-facing partner; Grace manages the accounts.
Extramarital affair. Duration unknown, at least several months. Victor Kasonde was aware of the relationship.
Mwape employed Kasonde as house-band musician. Kasonde was also blackmailing her at K50 per month over the embezzlement and the affair.
Relationship of fourteen months. Lungu was unaware of the blackmail arrangement or the specifics of what Kasonde had discovered.
Mutale acted as Kasonde's informal booking agent. Unpaid commission of K40 was in dispute at the time of Kasonde's death.
Musonda extended a K500 personal loan to Kasonde in November 1973. Kasonde repaid in full on 14 November 1974, the day of his murder.
Public dispute on 11 November 1974 over a composition Kabwe alleged Kasonde had stolen. Multiple witnesses present. Dispute was ongoing at time of death.
Bandmates in Broken String for three years. Close personal friendship. Emmanuel was the first to report the missing E-string to CID.
Zulu was coordinating a Radio Zambia studio session and potential vinyl pressing for Broken String. Met Kasonde privately twice in the week before his death.
Nsofu employed as head bouncer at The Copperbelt Room. On the night of the murder, Grace Mwape paid him fifty ngwee to vacate the front entrance on a false pretext.
Bwalya handles commercial disputes in Kamwala district. Patel Brothers has been subject to multiple market disputes within Bwalya's caseload. Contact extends beyond official channels.

confidential_notes.content: Received visit from R. Patel (Patel Brothers Import Wholesale, Kamwala, Stand 44) regarding ongoing market dispute with the Zambia Co-operative Federation. Matter resolved informally. Payment of K200 received as a consultancy gratuity. No formal record to be filed.
Second informal settlement — Patel Brothers matter. K300 received. R. Patel states ZCF dispute fully resolved. No further action required. Memorandum for personal file only.

Patel Brothers — further consultancy gratuity, K200. New matter: ZCF inspectors threatening licence review of Stand 44. Advised R. Patel to file application with the district council rather than engage inspectors directly. My involvement in this matter is strictly advisory in nature.
Meeting with S. Patel at the Lusaka Club, 18:00. He raised the possibility of a more formal ongoing arrangement. I told him I could not
